name: Derrick May
hook: The second of the Belleville Three, whose "Strings of Life" is the record most often used to explain techno's emotional range.
blurb: May grew up in Belleville, Michigan, with Juan Atkins and Kevin Saunderson, and the three of them are called the Belleville Three for starting Detroit techno together. He is usually cast as the emotional side of techno next to Atkins' big ideas. Recording as Rhythim Is Rhythim, May's 1987 track "Strings of Life", on his own label, Transmat, used string-like synth sounds to make electronic music feel warm and joyful instead of cold, and helped drive the explosion of house music in Britain in 1987 and 1988. Transmat also became a starting point for later Detroit producers and others close to Chicago's scene.

signatureTracks.title: Strings of Life (Rhythim Is Rhythim)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Synthetic string stabs over a stripped drum pattern; the record most credited with giving techno an emotional register beyond function.
